published_prior_art.cite: HeurtebiseEtAl2026LiMVAM: full-pair LiMVAM identification under cross-view diversity, but no partial-calibration compatibility frontier.
ShimizuEtAl2011DirectLiNGAM and HeurtebiseEtAl2026LiMVAM: recursive residual closure for a selected true root, but not removed-set complete enumeration.
HeurtebiseEtAl2026LiMVAM: bivariate cross-view correlation-diversity identification condition.
HauserBuhlmann2014ActiveLearning and LindgrenEtAl2018CostAware concern intervention separators, not passive residual-witness hitting for numerical coefficient tuples.
No located partial-calibration LiMVAM ancestral-poset result; the construction is a direct invariant of the proposed frontier.
ChernozhukovHongTamer2007SetInference supplies general inversion and GhoshalHonorio2018LinearSEM supplies recursive finite-sample gaps, but neither the stated LiMVAM set target nor its margins.
WangEtAl2023EquivalenceEnumeration supplies polynomial-delay enumeration only for locally colored decomposable AND--OR equivalence.

novelty_flags.label: Theorem 1 and related_work
novelty_flags.one_line: Add Shimizu2012JointLiNGAM and ChenEtAl2024IndividualCausalStructureLearning as close shared-order/multi-individual comparators and distinguish their unpaired or shared-ICA mechanisms from selected paired covariance blocks.

soundness_flags.label: ass:cross-variable-disturbance-orthogonality
soundness_flags.one_line: The cited LiMVAM source assumes mutually independent disturbance components within each view, not the stronger all-cross-view condition Cov(epsilon_i^(a),epsilon_j^(b))=0 for every i!=j; retag and independently justify this restrictive componentwise cross-view assumption.

soundness_flags.label: thm:compatibility-frontier and project_justification
soundness_flags.one_line: Because the core adds the stronger cross-view cross-component orthogonality condition absent from the cited LiMVAM model, Heurtebise et al.'s full-pair theorem is not presently a corollary on its published class; prove inclusion/widen the theorem or state the comparison only on the narrower class.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:covariance-region-inversion
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The finite-radius Hausdorff and exact-poset guarantees assume positive feasibility and path-product separation margins.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The inversion and exact-poset conclusions hold conditionally on delta_feas>=kappa_feas>0 and delta_path>=kappa_path>0.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:2502.20115v4, the version explicitly named in the bibliography; the ICML proceedings text was not publicly retrievable
source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 3, “Model assumptions”; Section 4, Assumption “Correlation and diversity across views” and identifiability theorem
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The model states that components of each disturbance vector e^i are mutually independent for a given view, while cross-view correlations are essential; it does not state zero covariance between different disturbance coordinates across different views.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Either generalize the compatibility certificate to the cited LiMVAM cross-view dependence class or explicitly introduce and empirically motivate componentwise cross-view disturbance independence as the new model class, then restate the Heurtebise comparison as a same-class restriction.

Add Shimizu (2012) Joint Estimation of Linear Non-Gaussian Acyclic Models and Chen et al. (2024) Individual Causal Structure Learning from Population Data, with a precise paired-versus-unpaired and covariance-versus-ICA distinction.
Elevate the passive calibration-design theorem by proving a hardness or approximation result for the induced-view hitting problem, conditional on the output quotient oracle.

recommended_next_step: Revise the maintained LiMVAM class and comparator inclusion claim, then expand the multi-view prior-art survey before advancing to Stage 0.
